bull_bear.body:
- Debt funded via banks (cheapest), NCDs, CPs, NHB refinance (application pending); repaid high-cost NCDs, timed CP raise. One term loan at 7.25% this quarter.
- ROE 18%+, ROA 2.39%; tax ~21%. No buyback/dividend detail this call. Capital deployment is into the loan book + the one-time IT build.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Elevated prepayment/rundown** (INR 1,857 cr; part-prepay INR 1,072 cr) — the structural drag on AUM growth; management admits "we will have to work on this."
- **Widening rate gap vs banks** (>100 bps) — could accelerate BT-out if repo stays low.
- **IT rollout execution** across 245 branches in one quarter (bandwidth/handholding at scale) — Q2 disbursement (INR 3,000 cr) is the stress test.
- **Opex/cost-to-income creep** to ~19.5% pressuring ROA (2.53%→2.39%).
- **IT-sector employment** softness in Bengaluru (only ~6% exposure, no impact yet — watch).
- **Competitive intensity** from Bajaj Housing (25-30% growth, tech-led) and LIC HFL (main BT counterparties).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly transparent, granular, numbers-forward (Suresh Iyer walked through the rundown bridge line-by-line; CFO Abhishek Mishra on tax). Candid that conservatism has cost growth, and that prepayment is "hurting us." Credible on asset quality (the ~INR 20 cr-since-2001 write-off stat, contextualised honestly with the fraud/provision nuance). No over-promising; explicitly deferring higher-yield product launch to Board. Reassuring but not defensive on the IT rollout risk.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The AUM-growth "miss" is a prepayment story, not a demand or competition story** — disbursements +29%, BT-out flat; the annual→quarterly reset mechanically crashed tenures (EMI constant → more principal), inflating amortisation. This is partly self-inflicted by the reset design.
- **Rate cuts hurt retention here:** because banks passed ~115 bps of repo cuts vs CanFin's ~55 bps, the CanFin-vs-bank gap widened to >100 bps — a rare case where a rate-down cycle is a net negative (prepayment) for a prime HFC.
- **SENP is a feature, not a risk** — documented-income (ITR-verified), ~0.5% higher yield, and net margin-accretive even after higher (1.45-1.5%) NPA; the +44% SENP growth is a deliberate, positive mix shift.
- **~INR 20 cr credit write-offs in ~25 years** is a genuine underwriting-culture moat, but it caps growth (management concedes it) — the IT transformation is the attempt to grow faster without loosening credit.
- **Watch Q2 as the operational stress test** — holding INR 3,000 cr disbursement while cutting over 245 branches is the real proof point; a mid-Sept update is promised.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Longstanding legacy of over three decades with consistent implementation of best governance practices, building stakeholder trust.
- Strong promoter backing with a Board that proactively embraces statutory and regulatory reforms.
- Established Code of Conduct for senior management and directors, reinforcing ethical operations and accountability.

business.body:
- **Home Loans (HL):** INR 1,650 cr (+28%); salaried GNPA ~0.6-0.63%.
- **Non-Housing (NHL):** INR 958 cr (+32%) — growing faster; LAP/top-up.
- **Salaried vs SENP:** SENP disbursement +44% (vs salaried +21%). SENP is documented-income (2-3 yr ITR verified), NOT surrogate/assessed; SENP NPA ~1.45-1.5% but yields ~0.5% higher → net margin-accretive.
- **Geography:** all 6 zones positive; Karnataka +18% (lowest), Telangana higher. IT-sector customers only ~6% of book, and not from top IT majors (Infosys/Wipro/Cognizant) → limited layoff exposure.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **Exceptional underwriting discipline:** only ~INR 20 cr credit write-offs since 2001 (another ~INR 50-60 cr frauds held at 100% provision, still on book as NPA); management attributes it to conservative customer selection — explicitly acknowledging it has capped growth at times ("safe lending").
- **Canara Bank sponsorship** + low, T-bill/repo-linked (no MCLR) borrowing → 6.98% cost of funds, structurally cheap.
- **Sticky BT-out** (flat INR 408 cr) despite a widened rate gap vs banks — main competition is LIC HFL + Bajaj, rarely banks.
business.title: 6a. Moat & competitive position

business.body:

PSU) pressuring on rate. These are the cleanest listed reference points from the call.

business.body: Can Fin Homes Limited is a housing finance company primarily engaged in providing loans for the purchase, construction, and renovation of residential properties to individuals. The company operates through a network of branches across India, serving salaried and self-employed customers in the affordable and mid-income housing segments. It also accepts public deposits and raises funds through debt securities and bank borrowings to finance its lending operations.

latest_quarter.body:
- NIM 3.81% (guided 3.75%), spread 2.83%; yield 9.81% held through the reset + rate cut; blended ROI ~9.8% (range 8.4% best salaried >725 CIBIL/>25L, up to ~12.5% non-salaried-non-housing S3).
- **Rate-differential risk:** CanFin best rate 8.4% vs banks 7.15-7.25% — gap widened from ~55 bps to >100 bps, the key retention pressure (drives part-prepayment).
- Incremental bank funding at 7.25-7.5% (vs 6.95% LY) — but only on new loans; NIM defended via mix.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1FY27 (this):** Disb INR 2,609 cr (+29%, ahead of 2,500 plan; HL +28%, NHL +32%, SENP +44%). Rundown INR 1,857 cr (part-prepay INR 1,072 cr the culprit; BT-out flat 408). AUM growth 10.8%. NIM 3.81% (beat 3.75%), yield 9.81%, CoF 6.98%, spread 2.83%. GNPA ~375-380 cr (+~18 cr only). ROA 2.39%, ROE 18%+, C/I ~19%. IT: 5-branch pilot live 8-July, full 250-branch rollout this quarter. Guidance: AUM +14%, disb ~13,000 cr (Q2 3,000), NIM 3.81%+, credit cost 10 bps, ROA ~2.4%/ROE ~18%, C/I ~19.5%→18% (3yr), tax 21%.
- _next Q → check: did IT rollout hold Q2 disbursement at INR 3,000 cr (execution/bandwidth); part-prepayment trajectory (retention initiatives working?); AUM growth toward 14%; NIM held at 3.81%+; credit cost vs 10 bps; C/I vs 19.5%; any higher-yield product launched; rate-gap vs banks / BT-out; mid-Sept IT update._

outlook.body:
- **AUM growth: 14%** for FY27 (may need to push disbursements harder each quarter to offset higher rundown).
- **Disbursements: ~INR 13,000 cr** FY27 (willing to stretch to INR 13,200-13,400 cr); **Q2 target INR 3,000 cr** (held despite IT rollout).
- **NIM: maintain 3.81%+** (only marginal incremental borrowing-cost creep; product/segment-mix yield levers available).
- **Credit cost: ~10 bps** FY27 (confident; trends improving).
- **ROA ~2.4% / ROE ~18%** FY27 (aspiration reaffirmed).
- **Cost-to-income ~19.5%** FY27, targeting **~18% within ~3 years** as book grows over fixed IT cost.
- **Tax rate ~21%** FY27 (DTA benefits, stable).
- **IT (LOS/LMS) rollout to all 250 branches** before the Q2 earnings call (~Sept); mid-Sept public update planned.

- **IT-enabled product velocity:** new LOS/LMS/decision-engine lets CanFin launch higher-yield (11-13%) risk-based products faster (Board not yet decided) and compress TAT to close the gap vs Bajaj Housing.

deepdive.thesis: Clean, conservative HFC executing well on volumes but fighting a structural prepayment leak: Q1 disbursements INR 2,609 cr (+29% YoY, ahead of the INR 2,500 cr plan) yet AUM growth only inched to 10.8% because rundown rose to INR 1,857 cr — driven NOT by balance-transfer-out (stable at INR 408 cr) but by faster part-prepayment (INR 1,072 cr) after the annual→quarterly reset crashed tenures. NIM 3.81% (beat 3.75% guide), asset quality pristine (NPA up only ~INR 18 cr vs ~INR 45 cr cyclical LY; ~INR 20 cr total credit write-off since 2001), ROA 2.39%/ROE 18%+. The swing factor for FY27 is the LOS/LMS IT transformation rolling to all 250 branches this quarter and whether faster tech lets it push 20%+ disbursement growth to out-run prepayment and hit 14% AUM growth.
